transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… mostly work stuff, I guess. I’m a sales supervisor, and I keep making these stupid little mistakes on reports. Like I’ll copy the wrong numbers from the team dashboard, or I’ll miss a line in a procedure I’m supposed to be checking, even when I thought I went back over it.

It’s frustrating because it’s not like I don’t care. I’ll be sitting there thinking, “Okay, I checked this,” and then later someone points out something obvious. It’s been happening enough that I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or time with family and friends?

Um… I don’t know, not really? I mean, I get frustrated, especially when work stuff piles up, but I wouldn’t say I’m just sitting around feeling down all the time.

As far as enjoying things, I think I still do. Like if my family’s around or we’re doing something, I’m usually fine once I’m there. Although sometimes getting myself to actually go do the thing is a whole separate problem—sorry, I’m probably getting off track. But no, I haven’t really noticed losing interest in things in that way.
Have you been feeling more tired or lacking energy lately, even when you haven’t been doing much physically?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I get tired, but I don’t know if it’s more than normal. Some days after work I feel kind of wiped, but it’s also like… work is a lot of people asking me stuff all day, and then I get home and there’s the usual house stuff.

But even when I’m not doing anything physical—yeah, I don’t know. I haven’t really been tracking it. I wouldn’t say I’m constantly exhausted or anything. I guess I’d have to think about it more.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating or focusing on tasks, even when you’re not particularly tired?

Yeah, definitely. It’s not even just when I’m tired. Like I’ll be reviewing call notes or checking numbers, and someone across the room will say something—doesn’t even have to be to me—and suddenly my brain is over there instead.

Or I’ll have some random thought, like, “Did I remember to take care of that thing at home?” and then I’m halfway into that thought before I realize I stopped doing the report. It’s annoying because I don’t always notice right away. I’ll think I’m still working, but I’ve kind of drifted off.
Do you find it hard to focus or get distracted easily even when you’re not at work, like during conversations or while watching something on TV?

Yeah, I do. It’s probably not just work, I guess. Like if I’m watching something, I’ll suddenly realize I missed a chunk because I started thinking about some random thing I need to do at home.

And conversations too—well, I mean, not always, but if there’s something going on nearby, like someone talking in the next room or noise outside, my attention just kind of goes there before I even catch it. It’s similar to when I’m trying to review call notes or numbers at work and one conversation across the room pulls me off. Then I have to sort of back up and figure out what I missed.

Outside of work and home distractions, do you find yourself struggling to organize tasks, forgetting everyday things like appointments or errands, or avoiding tasks that require sustained mental effort, like filling out forms or planning something out?

Yeah, I do forget stuff like that. Not all the time, but enough that it causes problems. Like I’ll mean to return a call from my attorney, and then something else comes up—my kid asking me something, or I see something in the garage I was supposed to move—and then the call just disappears from my head.

Bills too. I’ll think, “I need to pay that tonight,” and then I don’t, and next thing I know there’s a late notice and I’m like, oh, right. And I’ve done it with my kids too, like telling them I’ll bring something home or pick something up, and then I forget until they ask me about it. That one makes me feel pretty bad, honestly.
Do you often feel restless, like you need to be moving or doing something, or find yourself fidgeting a lot without realizing it?

Yeah, I do. Sitting through a long meeting is probably the worst example. It’s like my body is buzzing on the inside, even if I’m trying to look like I’m paying attention.

I’ll shift around in the chair, tap my foot, mess with a pen—sometimes I don’t even realize I’m doing it until somebody looks over or the table starts shaking. And then I’m thinking about how I need to stop moving, which somehow makes it harder to sit still.

Sometimes I’ll make up a reason to get up, like I need water or I’m checking on something, just so I can move for a minute. Meetings at work can drag on forever too, especially when people start going off into side conversations—actually, I guess I do that sometimes too—but yeah, sitting still for too long feels really uncomfortable.
When did you first start noticing these kinds of issues with focus, forgetfulness, or restlessness? Were they something you experienced earlier in life, like when you were in school?

Yeah, I think it goes pretty far back. My mom still brings it up sometimes, actually—like, not in a mean way, more like “you were always like this.”

She kept getting notes from teachers when I was in elementary school. Stuff like I’d rush through my work, lose homework, talk when I wasn’t supposed to, or get reminded to stay in my seat. I remember some of that, but honestly she remembers it better than I do. I was probably more worried about recess or whatever toy I had at the time. But yeah, it wasn’t something that just started as an adult.
Have these issues with focus, forgetfulness, or restlessness ever significantly interfered with your success in school, at work, or in your relationships with others?

Yeah… it has. I mean, at work it’s gotten past just being annoying. My manager actually put it in a formal review, like that I wasn’t following through on things or that stuff was slipping. That was pretty embarrassing.

And at home, yeah, it causes fights. Not always big fights, but it builds up because people feel like they can’t count on me to do what I said I’d do. Like I’ll have good intentions, I’ll really mean it in the moment, and then… I don’t know, it just falls off my radar. Then it looks like I don’t care, even when I do.
